ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — John F. Kennedy Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care about three months after primary adrenal insufficiency was diagnosed during an adrenal crisis abroad: replacement doses, electrolytes and renin, cause, autoimmune screening, sick-day rules and emergency kit, and chronic low back pain. Concerns: He wants to understand his adrenal condition and to never again be as ill as he was abroad; He wants enough energy to keep a full working week, and to decide himself who knows about the diagnosis; He wants his back pain to stop limiting him and to rely less on the brace. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Scarlet fever in early childhood, with a month in the hospital
Colitis diagnosed at the Mayo Clinic, with bowel symptoms and weight loss in his teens
Steroid treatment for colitis during his college years, including steroids placed under the skin
Back injury in a college football game, with back pain since and a corset brace
Back worsened during wartime naval service, when the boat he commanded was sunk; malaria in the Pacific
Lumbar spine operation at New England Baptist Hospital; pain returned about six weeks later
Collapse in England with a diagnosis of Addison's disease; so ill on the voyage home that he received the last rites; treated in Boston with desoxycorticosterone pellets

tr.td: Establishing primary care about three months after primary adrenal insufficiency was diagnosed during an adrenal crisis abroad: replacement doses, electrolytes and renin, cause, autoimmune screening, sick-day rules and emergency kit, and chronic low back pain
Two-week review and endocrinology consultation, with a bone density scan
Six-week review after the dose changes: electrolytes, renin, repeat thyroid tests, and back pain
Nine-month review: replacement, thyroid, autoimmune screening, bone health, and back pain
Same-day sick visit for influenza with stress dosing of hydrocortisone

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement adjusted by clinical assessment at every visit (weight, blood pressure lying and standing, energy, salt craving, and signs of over- or under-replacement), with sodium, potassium and plasma renin to guide fludrocortisone; doses set with endocrinology
Endocrinology consultation to confirm the cause, set the replacement doses, review the thyroid results and bone health, and plan stress dosing and follow-up

Written sick-day rules (double the hydrocortisone for fever above 38 °C, triple it above 39 °C, and inject and seek emergency care if vomiting or unable to take tablets), an emergency hydrocortisone injection kit with training, a steroid emergency card and a medical ID, reviewed at every visit

Screening for associated autoimmune disease: 21-hydroxylase antibodies for the cause, TSH, free T4 and thyroid peroxidase antibodies, vitamin B12, A1c and celiac serology with total IgA at intake; TSH at least yearly afterwards, and the others yearly or with symptoms

Chronic low back pain: physical therapy with core strengthening, swimming, heat, and gradual weaning from the brace except on long journeys; acetaminophen as needed; no opioids; Oswestry Disability Index at each review; imaging only for red flags
Bone health: a bone density scan because of corticosteroid exposure in his teens and twenties, calcium and vitamin D from diet, weight-bearing exercise, and avoiding glucocorticoid over-replacement

Influenza: oseltamivir for five days, hydrocortisone doubled under the sick-day rules until a day without fever and then back to the usual dose, fluids with salt, and the emergency injection with a 911 call if he vomits or cannot take tablets

Autoimmune hypothyroidism: levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, started only after glucocorticoid replacement was secure; TSH 6 weeks after starting, again at 6 months, then yearly; target TSH 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L
No adrenal crisis and no emergency admission through nine months
No crisis or admission; one febrile illness managed at home with stress dosing
Hydrocortisone at the lowest dose that keeps him well, within 15 to 25 mg a day, with his weight back toward his usual 72 kg and no signs of over-replacement
Hydrocortisone 20 mg a day in three doses; weight 72.0 kg from 66.0; no signs of excess
Sodium and potassium normal, renin in the upper normal range, and no postural drop in blood pressure by the six-week review
Sodium 139, potassium 4.4 mmol/L; renin 2.6 ng/mL/h; no postural drop
He can state the sick-day rules and give the emergency injection by the two-week visit
Stated the rules and gave a practice injection on a trainer
Oswestry Disability Index below 20% by three months, with the brace used only for long travel
Oswestry 18% at three months; brace used only on long journeys
